steps: Compare surnames first. “Santiago” vs “Santos”: S-a-n-t match. The 5th letter is “i” vs “o”. i comes before o, so Santiago, Lea is 1st.
The other three are all “Santos”, so compare their first names letter by letter.
“Mar” vs “Maria”: after “Mar”, the first has nothing and the second has “i”. Nothing comes before something, so Santos, Mar B. is 2nd.
“Maria” vs “Mario”: M-a-r-i match. The 5th letter is “a” vs “o”. a comes before o, so Maria is 3rd and Mario is 4th.
Order: Santiago, Lea; Santos, Mar B.; Santos, Maria L.; Santos, Mario A. The third is Santos, Maria L.

This is 2nd: “Mar” runs out before “Maria”, and nothing comes before something.
This is 4th (last): “Mario” has o where “Maria” has a, and a comes first.

82.tip: Compare one letter at a time; a name that runs out first goes first.

steps: Split the original into groups: PH | 4813 | QX7.
Check each option group by group against PH, 4813 and QX7.
Only PH-4813-QX7 matches all three groups exactly.

wrong.PH-4831-QX7: Middle group is 4831, not 4813: the last two digits 1 and 3 are swapped.
wrong.PH-4813-OX7: Last group starts with the letter O, not Q. Q has a small tail; O does not.
wrong.PH-4318-QX7: Middle group is 4318, not 4813: the 8 and the 3 are swapped.

83.tip: Check one group at a time, and watch look-alikes such as O/Q and O/0.

steps: Split each address into parts: barangay and city.
Barangay: “Brgy. San Isidro” vs “Brgy. San Isidro”. Same.
City: “Tagum City” vs “Tagum Ctiy”. Look at the letters: C-i-t-y vs C-t-i-y. The 2nd and 3rd letters (i and t) are swapped.
Only the city part is different.

wrong.Exactly alike: Not alike: “City” is spelled “Ctiy” in the second address.
wrong.Different in the barangay: Both say “Brgy. San Isidro” letter for letter.
wrong.Different in both: Only the city differs; the barangay is the same.

84.tip: Read slowly, letter by letter; swapped letters are easy to miss.

steps: The dates are written month/day/year. Compare the year first.
Two dates are in 2023 (12/01/2023 and 11/28/2023); the other two are in 2024, so they are later.
Between the 2023 dates, compare the month: 11 (November) comes before 12 (December).
So 11/28/2023 (November 28, 2023) is the earliest.

wrong.12/01/2023: Same year as the answer, but month 12 (December) comes after month 11 (November).
wrong.01/30/2024: January is an early month, but the year 2024 is later than 2023. Year comes first.

85.tip: For dates, compare year first, then month, then day.

steps: Count each word separately, including capital A.
“Accountability”: A-c-c-o-u-n-t-a-b-i-l-i-t-y. The capital A at the start and the a after “t” = 2.
“and”: a-n-d = 1.
“transparency”: t-r-a-n-s-p-a-r-e-n-c-y. The a after “tr” and the a after “sp” = 2.

wrong.4: Too few. This usually happens when you skip the capital A at the start of “Accountability”.
wrong.7: Too many. There are only 5 a's: 2 in Accountability, 1 in and, 2 in transparency.

86.tip: Count word by word, write each count down, then add.

steps: Split the original at the commas: 7 | 040 | 318.
Check each option group by group.
Only 7,040,318 has 7, then 040, then 318.

wrong.7,040,381: Last group is 381, not 318: the 1 and 8 are swapped.
wrong.7,004,318: Middle group is 004, not 040: the 0 and 4 are swapped.
wrong.7,400,318: Middle group is 400, not 040: the 4 moved to the front.

87.tip: Compare numbers one comma group at a time.

steps: All four start with “Department of”, so skip that and compare the next word.
The words are Education, Energy, Finance, Health. E comes before F and H.
Education vs Energy: both start with E. The 2nd letter is “d” vs “n”. d comes before n.
Order: Education, Energy, Finance, Health. Department of Education is first.

wrong.Department of Health: H comes after E and F, so Health is last.
wrong.Department of Finance: F comes after E, so Finance is 3rd.
wrong.Department of Energy: “En” comes after “Ed” (n is after d), so Energy is 2nd.

88.tip: Skip the words that are the same; the first different letter decides.

steps: Compare surnames first: Ramil, Ramirez, Ramos, Ramos.
“Ramil” vs “Ramirez”: R-a-m-i match. The 5th letter is “l” vs “r”. l comes before r, so Ramil is 1st and Ramirez is 2nd.
“Ramirez” vs “Ramos”: R-a-m match. The 4th letter is “i” vs “o”. i comes first, so both Ramos names come after Ramirez.
The two Ramos names have the same surname, so compare first names: “Carlo” vs “Celia”. The 2nd letter is “a” vs “e”. a comes first.
Order: Ramil, Teo; Ramirez, Jose; Ramos, Carlo; Ramos, Celia. The last is Ramos, Celia.

wrong.Ramil, Teo: This is 1st: “Ramil” (l) comes before “Ramirez” (r) and “Ramos” (o after i).
wrong.Ramos, Carlo: This is 3rd: same surname as Celia, but “Ca” comes before “Ce”.

170.tip: When surnames are the same, the first name decides.

steps: Split the original into groups: 482 | 305 | 117 | 000.
Check each option group by group.
Only TIN 482-305-117-000 matches all four groups.

wrong.TIN 482-305-171-000: Third group is 171, not 117: the 1 and 7 are swapped.
wrong.TIN 482-350-117-000: Second group is 350, not 305: the 0 and 5 are swapped.
wrong.TIN 428-305-117-000: First group is 428, not 482: the 8 and 2 are swapped.

171.tip: Check long ID numbers one dash group at a time.

steps: Split each name into parts: surname, first name, middle initial.
Surname: “Dela Cruz” vs “Dela Cruz”. Same.
First name: N-o-r-b-e-r-t-o vs N-o-b-e-r-t-o. The 3rd letter “r” is missing in the second name.
Middle initial: “M.” vs “M.”. Same. So only the first name differs.

wrong.Exactly alike: Not alike: “Noberto” is missing the first r of “Norberto”.
wrong.Different in surname: Both surnames are “Dela Cruz” letter for letter.

172.tip: Compare a name part by part: surname, first name, middle initial.

steps: Both ends start with 2045, so the answer must also start with 2045.
Now the second group must be between 118 and 131.
Check: 110 is below 118; 132 is above 131; 125 is between (118 < 125 < 131).
So 2045-125 fits.

wrong.2045-110: 110 is less than 118, so it comes before 2045-118, not after.
wrong.2045-132: 132 is more than 131, so it comes after 2045-131.
wrong.2054-120: The first group is 2054, not 2045 (4 and 5 swapped). It is a different series and comes after all 2045 files.

173.tip: Check the first group first; only then look at the second group.

steps: Count each group separately.

wrong.5: Too few. Recount: 7471 has 2, 7077 has 3, 1717 has 2.
wrong.6: One short. People often count only 2 sevens in 7077, but it has 3.

174.tip: Count each group on its own, write the number down, then add.

steps: Letter by letter means you compare the names exactly as spelled. “Mc” is M-c, not “Mac”.
2nd letters: Mabini (a), Macaraeg (a), Magsaysay (a), McArthur (c). The three with “a” come before McArthur.
3rd letters of the “Ma” names: Mabini (b), Macaraeg (c), Magsaysay (g). b comes first.
Order: Mabini, Macaraeg, Magsaysay, McArthur. Mabini is first.

wrong.McArthur: Its 2nd letter is c, which comes after a, so it is last. Do not read “Mc” as “Mac”.
wrong.Macaraeg: Its 3rd letter is c, which comes after the b in Mabini, so it is 2nd.
wrong.Magsaysay: Its 3rd letter is g, which comes after b and c, so it is 3rd.

175.tip: Letter by letter: file names exactly as spelled (Mc = M-c).

steps: Split each line into two parts: reference number and amount.
Reference: “00918-AX” vs “00918-AX”. Same.
Amount: ₱12,450.75 vs ₱12,540.75. The “12” and “.75” match, but the middle group is 450 vs 540: the 4 and 5 are swapped.
Only the amount is different.

wrong.Different in both: Only the amount changed; the reference number is the same.

176.tip: In money amounts, check every digit group; swapped digits change the value.

steps: All dates are in 2025, so compare the months: January, then February, then March.
Two dates are in March: March 1 and March 3. Day 1 comes before day 3.
Order: January 30, February 28, March 1, March 3.
The third date is March 1, 2025.

wrong.March 3, 2025: This is 4th (last): it is after March 1.
wrong.January 30, 2025: This is 1st: January is the earliest month.
wrong.February 28, 2025: This is 2nd: February comes after January but before March.

177.tip: Same year: compare months. Same month: compare days.

steps: “Villa” vs “Villamor”: after “Villa”, the first has nothing and the second has “m”. Nothing comes before something, so Villa, Teo is 1st.
“Villamor” vs “Villanueva”: after “Villa”, the next letter is “m” vs “n”. m comes before n, so Villamor, Ana is 2nd.
The two Villanueva names: “Carla” vs “Carlo”. After “Carl”, it is “a” vs “o”. a comes first.
Order: Villa, Teo; Villamor, Ana; Villanueva, Carla; Villanueva, Carlo. Second is Villamor, Ana.

wrong.Villa, Teo: This is 1st: “Villa” ends where the others continue, and nothing comes before something.
wrong.Villanueva, Carlo: This is 4th: same surname as Carla, but “Carlo” (o) comes after “Carla” (a).

178.tip: Nothing comes before something: Villa goes before Villamor.

steps: Compare surnames first: three are “Domingo” and one is “Dominguez”.
“Domingo” vs “Dominguez”: D-o-m-i-n-g match. The 7th letter is “o” vs “u”. o comes before u, so every Domingo comes before Dominguez.
Inside Domingo, compare first names: Ramon (Ra) comes first; then “Renato” vs “Rene”: after “Ren”, it is “a” vs “e”, so Renato comes before Rene.
Order: Domingo, Ramon; Domingo, Renato; Domingo, Rene; Dominguez, Ana. The last is Dominguez, Ana.

wrong.Domingo, Ramon: This is 1st: Domingo surname, and “Ra” comes before “Re”.
wrong.Domingo, Rene: This is 3rd: it is last among the Domingo names, but every Domingo comes before Dominguez.

179.tip: Surname first; the first name matters only when surnames are the same.

steps: Split the original into groups: 34 | 5678912 | 3.
Check each option group by group; read the long middle group in small chunks: 567-891-2.
Only 34-5678912-3 matches every group.

wrong.34-5678921-3: Middle group ends in 21, not 12: the last two digits are swapped.
wrong.34-5687912-3: Middle group starts 5687, not 5678: the 7 and 8 are swapped.
wrong.43-5678912-3: First group is 43, not 34: the 3 and 4 are swapped.

180.tip: Break long numbers into small chunks and compare chunk by chunk.

steps: Split the original into groups: 0045 | 2210 | 98.
Check each option group by group.
Only 0045-2210-98 matches all three groups.

wrong.0045-2201-98: Middle group is 2201, not 2210: the 1 and 0 are swapped.
wrong.0054-2210-98: First group is 0054, not 0045: the 4 and 5 are swapped.
wrong.0045-2210-89: Last group is 89, not 98: the 9 and 8 are swapped.

181.tip: Compare account numbers one dash group at a time.

steps: Split each address into parts: purok, barangay, city.
Purok: “Purok 5” vs “Purok 5”. Same.
Barangay: “Brgy. Apokon” vs “Brgy. Apokon”. Same.
City: “Tagum City” vs “Tagum City”. Same. Every character matches.

wrong.Different in the barangay: Both say Brgy. Apokon, letter for letter.
wrong.Different in the city: Both say Tagum City, letter for letter.

182.tip: Do not assume there must be a difference; sometimes both are identical.

steps: Split each entry into two parts: name and number.
Name: “Juan P. Reyes” vs “Juan P. Reyes”. Same.
Number groups: 0917 = 0917, 123 = 123, but 4567 vs 4576: the last two digits 6 and 7 are swapped.
Only the number is different.

wrong.Exactly alike: Not alike: the last group is 4567 in one and 4576 in the other.
wrong.Different in the name: Both names are “Juan P. Reyes” exactly.
wrong.Different in both: Only the number differs; the name is the same.

183.tip: Check phone numbers group by group, especially the last digits.

steps: Write out the letters: E-X-C-E-L-L-E-N-C-E.
Mark each E: 1st letter, 4th letter, 7th letter, 10th letter.
That is 4 E's.

wrong.3: One short. People often miss the last E at the end of the word.
wrong.5: Too many. Only the 1st, 4th, 7th and 10th letters are E.
wrong.6: Too many. The word has 10 letters and only 4 of them are E.

184.tip: Spell the word out letter by letter and tick each match.

steps: Compare years first: three dates are in 2026 and one (July 1, 2025) is in 2025. 2026 is later.
Among the 2026 dates, compare months: May comes before June.
Two dates are in June: June 3 and June 30. Day 30 is after day 3.
So June 30, 2026 is the latest.

wrong.July 1, 2025: July is a later month, but the year 2025 is earlier than 2026. Year comes first.
wrong.May 31, 2026: May comes before June in the same year.
wrong.June 3, 2026: Same month as the answer, but day 3 is before day 30.

185.tip: Latest date: biggest year, then biggest month, then biggest day.

steps: All four numbers start with 1, so look at the 2nd digit: 1048 (0), 1084 (0), 1408 (4), 1004 (0). 1408 has the biggest, so it is highest.
For the three that start with 10, look at the 3rd digit: 1004 (0), 1048 (4), 1084 (8).
Order from lowest: 1004, 1048, 1084, 1408.
The second is 1048.

wrong.1004: This is the lowest (1st): its 3rd digit is 0.
wrong.1084: This is 3rd: its 3rd digit 8 is bigger than the 4 in 1048.
wrong.1408: This is the highest (4th): its 2nd digit is 4, while the others have 0.

186.tip: Same number of digits: compare from the left, one digit at a time.

steps: Check each pair: compare the letters, then the four digits.
XZ-9087 / XZ-9078: letters match and “90” matches, but then 87 vs 78: the 8 and 7 are swapped.
So XZ-9087 and XZ-9078 is the pair that is NOT alike.

wrong.AB-1234 and AB-1234: Both sides are identical, letter for letter and digit for digit.

187.tip: For “NOT alike”, hunt for the one pair with any difference.

steps: Ask: what is this memo mainly about? Leave credits are the vacation and sick leave days that employees earn.
Personnel (human resources) files hold records about employees: hiring, appointments, attendance, leave and benefits.
So a memo on employee leave credits goes under Personnel.

wrong.Procurement: Procurement is for buying supplies, equipment and services, not employee leave.
wrong.Finance: Finance is for budgets, payments and disbursements. Leave credits are counted in days and kept in employee records.
wrong.Legal: Legal is for cases, contracts and legal opinions.

188.tip: If it is about employees, file it under Personnel.

steps: Ask: what is this record mainly about? A purchase request asks the office to buy something (printer ink).
Procurement files hold records of buying goods and services: purchase requests, canvass, bids and purchase orders.
So the purchase request goes under Procurement.

wrong.Personnel: Personnel is for employee records such as leave and appointments.
wrong.Training: Training is for seminars, workshops and learning programs.
wrong.Legal: Legal is for cases, contracts and legal opinions.

189.tip: Anything about buying goes under Procurement.

steps: Rule: “i before e, except after c.”
In this word the letters come right after “c”, so write e first, then i: c-e-i.
Correct spelling: R-E-C-E-I-V-E.

wrong.Recieve: The i and e are reversed after c; after c it is “ei”.
wrong.Receeve: It has a double e and no i.

190.tip: i before e, except after c: rec-EI-ve.

steps: All four start with “Bureau of”, so compare the next word: Corrections, Customs, Fire Protection, Immigration.
Two start with C. “Corrections” vs “Customs”: the 2nd letter is “o” vs “u”. o comes before u, so Corrections is 1st and Customs is 2nd.
Then F (Fire Protection) is 3rd and I (Immigration) is 4th.
The second is Bureau of Customs.

wrong.Bureau of Fire Protection: This is 3rd: F comes after C.
wrong.Bureau of Immigration: This is 4th: I comes after C and F.

191.tip: Skip the shared words; the first different letter decides.

steps: Count each group separately.

wrong.5: Too few. Recount: 1005 has 2, 2030 has 2, 4000 has 3.
wrong.6: One short. A common slip is missing the last 0 in 2030.

192.tip: Count each group on its own, write it down, then add.

steps: Split each line into parts: room, floor, building.
Room: “Rm. 214” vs “Rm. 241”. The 1 and 4 are swapped.
Floor: “2nd Flr.” vs “2nd Flr.”. Same.
Building: “Capitol Bldg.” vs “Capitol Bldg.”. Same. Only the room number differs.
193.tip: Compare part by part; one swapped digit is enough to make them different.

steps: Rule: sort by letter first. The A codes (A-30, A-4) come before the B codes (B-12, B-2).
Inside the A codes, sort the numbers by value: 4 is smaller than 30.
Order: A-4, A-30, B-2, B-12. A-4 is first.

wrong.A-30: This is 2nd. Its first digit 3 looks smaller than 4, but the rule says numerical order, and 30 is bigger than 4.
wrong.B-2: This is 3rd: every A code comes before any B code.
wrong.B-12: This is 4th (last): it is a B code, and 12 is bigger than 2.

194.tip: Letter first, then number by its full value (4 before 30).

steps: AM means before noon (morning). PM means after noon. 12:15 PM is 15 minutes after noon.
8:45 AM, 9:30 AM and 11:50 AM are all in the morning, before noon.
So 12:15 PM is the latest.

wrong.8:45 AM: This is the earliest of the four.
wrong.9:30 AM: Still in the morning, before noon.
wrong.11:50 AM: Close, but it is 10 minutes before noon, 25 minutes earlier than 12:15 PM.

195.tip: 12 PM is noon; a PM time is later than any AM time on the same day.

steps: Split the original into parts: Ma. | Cristina | B. | Gonzales.
Check each option part by part: first name C-r-i-s-t-i-n-a, middle initial B., surname ending in s.
Only Ma. Cristina B. Gonzales matches every part.

wrong.Ma. Christina B. Gonzales: First name has an extra h: “Chr” instead of “Cr”.
wrong.Ma. Cristina B. Gonzalez: Surname ends in z instead of s.
wrong.Ma. Cristina D. Gonzales: Middle initial is D instead of B.

196.tip: Check names part by part, including small endings like s/z.

steps: Check each pair letter by letter.
Tagum / Tagun: the last letter is m vs n. Panabo / Panobo: the 4th letter is a vs o. Carmen / Carmin: the 5th letter is e vs i.
Davao del Norte / Davao del Norte: every letter matches.
So the Davao del Norte pair is exactly alike.

wrong.Tagum and Tagun: The last letter differs: m vs n.
wrong.Panabo and Panobo: The 4th letter differs: a vs o.
wrong.Carmen and Carmin: The 5th letter differs: e vs i.

197.tip: Watch look-alike letters such as m/n, a/o and e/i.

steps: Letter by letter means you ignore the spaces and read each surname as one word.
Del Rosario = DELROSARIO, Dela Cruz = DELACRUZ, De Leon = DELEON, Delgado = DELGADO.
The first three letters D-E-L are the same in all. Look at the 4th letter: R, A, E, G.
Alphabet order: A, E, G, R. So the order is Dela Cruz, De Leon, Delgado, Del Rosario. Dela Cruz is first.

wrong.Del Rosario, Ben: Its 4th letter is R, the latest of the four, so it is last.
wrong.De Leon, Carlo: This is 2nd: its 4th letter is E (DELE...). The space after “De” does not count in letter-by-letter filing.
wrong.Delgado, Rita: This is 3rd: its 4th letter is G, which comes after A and E.

333.tip: Letter by letter: drop the spaces and compare as one word.

steps: All surnames are “Santos”, so compare what comes after: Jose, Jose Jr., Joseph, Josefa.
All start with “Jose”. After “Jose”, plain “Jose” has nothing, while the others have more (Jr., p, fa).
Nothing comes before something, so Santos, Jose comes first.

Same name plus “Jr.”. Plain “Jose” has nothing after it, so it goes ahead of “Jose Jr.”.
wrong.Santos, Joseph: After “Jose”, Joseph still has “ph”. Nothing comes before something.
wrong.Santos, Josefa: After “Jose”, Josefa still has “fa”. Nothing comes before something.

334.tip: Nothing comes before something: the shortest matching name goes first.

steps: Alphabetic filing arranges records by name, A to Z.
Numeric filing arranges records by number, such as file or case numbers.
Geographic filing arranges records by place: region, province, city or barangay.
Chronological filing arranges records by date. So the system based on place is Geographic.

wrong.Alphabetic: Sorts by name, A to Z, not by place.
wrong.Numeric: Sorts by assigned numbers, not by place.
wrong.Chronological: Sorts by date, not by place.

steps: Chronological filing arranges records by date, oldest to newest or newest to oldest.
Subject filing groups records by topic; geographic by place; alphanumeric by codes that mix letters and numbers.
So the system based on date is Chronological.

wrong.Subject: Groups records by topic (e.g. Personnel, Procurement), not by date.
wrong.Geographic: Groups records by place, not by date.
wrong.Alphanumeric: Sorts by codes that mix letters and numbers (e.g. A-12), not by date.

336.tip: Chrono = time, so chronological = by date.

steps: The usual order of a business letter: heading/date, inside address, salutation, body, complimentary close, signature line.
The salutation is the greeting, such as “Dear Sir:”.
It comes right before the body, so Salutation is the answer.

wrong.Inside address: It comes before the salutation, so it is two steps before the body.
wrong.Complimentary close: It comes after the body (e.g. “Very truly yours,”).
wrong.Signature line: It comes at the very end, after the complimentary close.

337.tip: Greet (salutation), talk (body), say goodbye (close), then sign.

steps: In the full block style, every part (date, inside address, salutation, body, closing and signature) starts at the left margin.
There are no indented paragraphs and nothing is centered or pushed to the right.
So “Every line starts at the left margin” is correct.

wrong.The date is centered: In full block the date is also at the left margin. A centered or right-side date belongs to other styles, such as modified block.
wrong.Paragraphs are indented: Indented paragraphs belong to the semi-block style, not full block.
wrong.The closing is on the right: A closing toward the right belongs to the modified block style; in full block it is at the left margin.

steps: “CONFIDENTIAL” means the content is private or sensitive.
Only people who are authorized and need the information for their work may see it.
So it should be shown only to authorized persons and kept secure.

wrong.Posted on the bulletin board: A bulletin board is public; this is the opposite of confidential.
wrong.Shared with all staff: Not all staff are authorized; confidential means limited access.
wrong.Thrown away after reading: Confidential records must be kept safely; they can be disposed of only under the proper retention and disposal rules.

steps: Active records are used often and are kept in the office for easy access.
Inactive records are seldom used but must still be kept until their retention period ends, usually in storage.
Vital records are essential for the agency to keep running or to protect rights; draft records are unfinished versions.
Records that are seldom used but must be kept for a set period are Inactive records.

wrong.Active records: Active records are used often, not seldom.
wrong.Vital records: Vital records are defined by importance (the agency cannot function without them), not by how seldom they are used.
wrong.Draft records: Drafts are unfinished versions of documents, not stored records awaiting their retention period.

340.tip: Active = used often; inactive = rarely used but still kept.

steps: Split the original: 12 | 050478291 | 6.
Break the long middle group into chunks of three: 050 | 478 | 291.
Compare each option chunk by chunk. Only 12-050478291-6 matches all chunks.

wrong.12-050478219-6: Last chunk is 219, not 291: the 9 and 1 are swapped.
wrong.12-050487291-6: Middle chunk is 487, not 478: the 7 and 8 are swapped.
wrong.12-005478291-6: First chunk is 005, not 050: the 0 and 5 are swapped.

341.tip: Break long numbers into chunks of three, then compare chunk by chunk.

steps: Check each pair digit by digit.
BDO-4471 / BDO-4471: alike. LBP-1188 / LBP-1188: alike.
PNB-9032 / PNB-9023: the last two digits 3 and 2 are swapped. Not alike.
DBP-5605 / DBP-5650: the last two digits 0 and 5 are swapped. Not alike.
Alike pairs: BDO and LBP = 2.

wrong.1: Too few: both the BDO and the LBP pairs match exactly.
wrong.3: Too many: PNB (9032 vs 9023) and DBP (5605 vs 5650) both have swapped digits.
wrong.4: That would mean all pairs match, but the PNB and DBP pairs do not.

342.tip: Mark each pair alike or not alike, then count the marks.

steps: Rule: sort by the first number (by value), then by the second number.
First numbers: 2, 2, 12, 2. Since 2 is less than 12, all the “2-” files come before 12-001.
Among the “2-” files, compare the second numbers by value: 041 (41), 104, 140. 41 < 104 < 140.

wrong.2-104: This is 2nd: 104 is bigger than 41 but smaller than 140.
wrong.2-041: This is 1st: 41 is the smallest second number among the “2-” files.
wrong.12-001: This is last: 12 is bigger than 2, even though it starts with the digit 1.

343.tip: Compare numbers by their full value, not by their first digit.

steps: Break the word down: re + commend + ation.
“Commend” has one c and two m's: c-o-m-m-e-n-d.
So the correct spelling is R-E-C-O-M-M-E-N-D-A-T-I-O-N: one c, double m, and “e” after the m's.

wrong.Reccomendation: It doubles the c and uses only one m; it should be one c and two m's.
wrong.Recommandation: It has “a” after the m's instead of “e” (that is the French spelling).

344.tip: Recommend = re + commend: one c, two m's.

steps: A memorandum (memo) is a short written message used inside an office or agency.
It is used for announcements, instructions, reminders and policies sent to employees or other units of the same organization.
So its main use is communication within an office or agency.

wrong.Letters to foreign governments: Communication with other governments is external and uses formal letters or diplomatic notes, not memos.
wrong.Personal letters: Personal letters are private, not official office communication.
wrong.Court decisions: Court decisions are issued by courts as rulings, not as office memos.

345.tip: Memo = inside the office; letter = outside.

steps: The receiving stamp records the exact date and time the office got the letter.
That date is the starting point for counting the deadline to act or reply. Under RA 6713, offices must respond within 15 working days.
With the stamp, anyone can check whether the letter was acted on in time.

wrong.Make it look official: The stamp is not decoration; its purpose is to record when the letter was received.
wrong.Replace the signature: A receiving stamp cannot take the place of the sender's or an official's signature.
wrong.Mark it as confidential: Confidentiality is marked separately (e.g. “CONFIDENTIAL”); the receiving stamp only records receipt.

346.tip: The receiving stamp starts the clock.
